tickets.title: 11th Street delivery worker bike obstruction
tickets.requester: Chris Messb (public speaker); Keith Powers (State Assembly Member); District manager (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Residents and businesses report over 100 electric delivery bikes stored on the sidewalk and street at 11th Street and 1st Avenue, around the clock, which has closed businesses and obstructed the block. The district manager has worked on the issue since February 2024, and the precinct plans a confiscation enforcement action on October 7 while outreach groups ask for tagging instead and translated notices. Action: The district office should follow up with the precinct and agencies on the October 7 enforcement, the translated warnings for drivers, and the sanitation and storage options raised in the meeting.

tickets.title: Seward Park drug activity and dark lighting
tickets.summary: Speakers report increased drug use, more homeless people, and poorly lit dark spots in Seward Park, and the Seward Park Conservancy and Lower East Side Ecology Center complained about drug use near their building. Outreach providers and police are active, and a speaker asked whether mobile crisis teams could be expanded to reduce drug use in the park instead of relying on police. Action: The district office should ask the Parks Department and DOT to fix the lights and should ask the precinct and city outreach providers how mobile crisis teams could address drug use in Seward Park.

tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker who ran a simulation of MTA trip data argued that closing the L train stop at Third Avenue would save New Yorkers about 1,800 hours a day because few riders board or alight there and it is not a transfer or wheelchair-accessible station. Action: The board should refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about piloting the closure of the Third Avenue stop.

tickets.title: East River Pier roller skating venue proposal
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot multi-use indoor roller skating building on the East River Pier to replace closed rinks, with low admission and projected hundreds of jobs. The proposal was presented without any board action requested in the meeting. Action: The board should review the pier proposal and decide whether to take a position on it.

tickets.title: NYCHA food, necessities, and deaf communication access
tickets.summary: A NYCHA resident said residents in poverty lack food, water, and necessities and asked what the community can do about it. He also said deaf and hard of hearing residents need communication access, and that drugs and toxicity should be removed from the community. Action: The district office should follow up with the appropriate agencies on food and necessities assistance for NYCHA residents and on communication access for deaf residents.

tickets.title: MetroCard support for Immigrant Welcome Center access
tickets.requester: Harlem resident (unnamed public speaker); Niles Robinson (Public Advocate office liaison)
tickets.summary: A speaker asked whether MetroCards or other fare support will be available for people who must travel uptown, often with multiple transfers, to reach the new Immigrant Welcome Center on 125th Street. The liaison said the question would be raised with the office. Action: The Public Advocate office liaison should raise the transportation cost question for the welcome center with the office.

tickets.title: Public restroom pilot locations and access rules
tickets.location_raw: Delansancy Plaza and Cooper Square at East Sixth Street
tickets.requester: Obie (Mayor's Office representative); Transportation committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: The city is installing free public restrooms as a one-year pilot, with two sites in the district at Delansancy Plaza and Cooper Square at East Sixth Street. Concerns were raised about who can access them and about emergency calls, and the Mayor's Office asked for suggested nonprofit or good locations. Action: The board should vote on a resolution next month to set out access and emergency procedures for the restroom pilot.

tickets.title: Canal Street redesign phase two update
tickets.summary: The board sent a letter asking for an update on the Canal Street redesign project because no update has been given since January. Phase two in the district is still pending community input. Action: The board should follow up with DOT to obtain the Canal Street redesign update and provide community input on phase two.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits safety concerns
tickets.summary: The transportation committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating community concerns at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge, following prior resolutions and a recent fatal crash. Action: The board should follow up with the mayor and DOT on the letter and request an update on changes at the Manhattan Bridge exits.

tickets.title: Transportation equity analysis with IBO
tickets.summary: The transportation committee met with the Independent Budget Office in the summer to compare district transportation service with other districts, and narrowed ten ideas to three priorities, including cross-town buses and neighborhood parking locations. Action: The district office should obtain the IBO research on cross-town bus service and neighborhood parking locations for the committee.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR reporting
tickets.summary: A board member asked whether the congestion pricing impacts projected for the FDR, identified in the air quality report and an earlier resolution, actually occurred. The transportation chair agreed to follow up on it. Action: The board should request that MTA or DOT report on actual congestion impacts on the FDR and whether reporting is planned.

tickets.title: Draft housing plan affordable housing comments
tickets.summary: The city's draft housing plan proposes about 7,000 units for the district over five years, but 75 percent are market rate, while the board's top need is affordable housing. The board commented on the draft with little time, and members asked for ongoing engagement. Action: The land use committee should take proactive positions on future housing plan drafts and seek ongoing engagement.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and clarification
tickets.summary: The land use and economic development committees passed two resolutions asking EDC to postpone issuing the Essex Market RFP so it keeps a community market, but EDC was not prepared to say whether its resolutions were included. The RFP was due to go out at the end of this month. Action: The land use committee should meet with EDC this week to clarify whether the resolutions were incorporated and ask EDC to postpone the RFP.

tickets.title: 11 Allen Street full liquor license denial
tickets.requester: Michelle Cooper Smith (board member); Carlin Chan (board member)
tickets.summary: The SLA committee split 3 to 2 on a full liquor license application for 11 Allen Street, an operator tied to a problematic nearby location, and a member moved a straight denial. The full board voted 20 yes, 10 no, and 9 abstaining, so the recommendation is denial. Members warned that without community attendance at the SLA hearing the state could approve the license without stipulations. Action: The community board office should organize residents willing to attend the SLA hearing and support the denial, and members should watch the SLA calendar.

tickets.title: August SLA resolution wording corrections
tickets.summary: The chair reported two clerical errors in August SLA resolutions, number 3 for Cozy Cafe and number 10 for a tea house, where the text should refer to a beer and wine license rather than a full on-premises license. The errors were stated on the record. Action: None; the chair noted the corrections for the record.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election result
tickets.summary: The board held a special election for second vice chair between Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas after both gave speeches. Daniel Tano received 25 votes and Zachary Thomas received 14. Action: None; the election is complete and Daniel Tano was announced as second vice chair.

tickets.title: Board member mentor assignment for Leila Mahia
tickets.summary: The chair introduced new board member Leila Mahia. The board will assign a mentor to her in the near future. Action: The board office should assign a mentor to Leila Mahia.

tickets.title: SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures trainings
tickets.summary: The chair announced planned trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, with dates to be announced, to help new and returning members. The chair also said members should ask more questions in board discussions. Action: The chair should report training dates, and members should email the chair with training requests.

tickets.title: Attendance and bylaws revision proposal
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would address attendance by sending members a letter and meeting with the executive committee after excess absences, instead of using the removal process, and would require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. A member noted a double-recommendation wording issue. Action: The board should vote on the proposed bylaws at the October full board meeting after the 28-day notice is emailed to members.

tickets.title: Mobile voting pilot for school community education council elections
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee representative (unnamed); Troy (board member)
tickets.summary: The health and human services committee presented a resolution urging the NYC Department of Education to pilot a mobile voting option for community education council elections, since turnout is about 2 percent and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers asked for clear immigration-privacy messaging, multilingual outreach, and eligibility explanations. Action: The board should vote on the resolution urging the DOE to pilot mobile voting and expand outreach to parents.
